analysis.title: When Goldman & JPM Won't Hold It, Should You? The 11% AI Chip Loan Banks Refused To Underwrite
key_insights: JPMorgan and Goldman Sachs are joint lead arrangers on a $5.012B six-year financing for Volta Infrastructure Holdings, a neocloud founded this year, but underwrote only the $1.3B term loan C. The $3.712B GPU term loan is not underwritten (best-efforts), per Bloomberg.

The package prices at SOFR+625-650 with a 0% floor and OID of 97-98, for a yield to maturity of 11.21%-11.75% per PitchBook LCD. Bloomberg calls it one of the highest borrowing costs in the AI leveraged loan market.

The facilities are unrated, non-call for two years, then callable at 102 in year three and par in year four. Weighted average life is 3.1 years, with amortization sculpted to repay in full within 5.5 years of funding.

The $1.3B tranche cash-collateralizes a letter of credit for Volta's data-center lease with Bitdeer in Norway. The $3.712B tranche funds about 36,000 Nvidia GPUs. Bloomberg previously reported Anthropic signed a six-year compute agreement at the site.
Nvidia is listed among Volta's backers (PitchBook), so Nvidia is an investor in a company buying its chips with borrowed money. Other listed backers are a16z, Altimeter and Michael Dell.

Pricing compares with earlier neocloud deals: CoreWeave's $8.5B DDTL 4.0 in March was investment grade (A3 Moody's) at SOFR+225 floating and about 5.9% fixed. CoreWeave's $2.6B DDTL 5.5 in July was flexed from S+425-450 to S+550 at 97 OID, a 10.44% yield. Volta prices another 75-100bp wider.

Goldman credit strategists (Amanda Lynam, Oct 9) put US high yield all-in yield at 8.3%, up about 170bp YTD, and forecast US leveraged loan defaults around 5% in 2027, with recoveries around $56 versus $64 in 2022. Volta pays roughly 300bp over the high yield index.
CLOs, the largest buyers of leveraged loans, typically cannot buy an unrated loan like this one.

Hyperscaler credit is under strain: Meta's Hyperion SPV bonds (priced at 6.581% a year ago) hit a record low in price, Oracle long bonds trade above 8%, and Oracle data-center debt trades at junk spreads.

Evidence of bank caution cited: partial underwriting, syndication fatigue (the $38B Oracle-linked Texas/Wisconsin construction loan led by JPMorgan and MUFG still had under $1B unsold after six months), significant risk transfers explored by JPMorgan, Morgan Stanley, SMBC and MUFG as they approach internal AI exposure limits, and record CDS.

Oracle 5Y CDS was 257bp last Thursday, the widest since at least 2009 and up from 182bp in mid-September. Broadcom CDS is at a record 133bp and Nvidia is near its all-time high of 87bp. Part of the move is banks hedging loan books.
The GPU loan's 3.1-year WAL and 5.5-year full amortization imply lenders expect chips to hold value for less time than CoreWeave's six-year depreciation schedule.
Goldman's TMT desk said global equities weakened as investors continued to de-risk from AI-capex and AI-financing exposure.

Counterpoint: banks run an originate-to-distribute model, best-efforts syndication for a first-time unrated borrower is not unprecedented, and private credit and insurers keep funding AI deals, including a $42B Broadcom-backstopped senior secured loan for Anthropic that began syndication last Monday per IFR.

Goldman's Rich Privorotsky relayed Broadcom's Hock Tan as saying compute demand exceeds supply and frontier labs with substantial revenue can afford expensive financing. Privorotsky also says the market is still being bought on dips.
The Bank of England has warned that banks are exposed indirectly through lending to private credit funds.

JPMorgan CFO Jeremy Barnum said on the earnings call that the bank's AI exposure is diffused across construction loans, equity markets and working-capital revolvers, and that institutions will contain single-party risk.

The author sides with the skeptics: banks finance the AI boom but are shifting the risk to buyers. Volta's books close 5pm ET Oct 14, and the watch item is whether the GPU tranche is flexed wider, downsized or pushed into private credit.

sector_views.rationale: Banks are limiting underwriting, spreads and CDS are widening, and risk is moving to buyers demanding about 11%.

earnings_insights: JPMorgan CFO Jeremy Barnum on the Oct 13 earnings call: the bank's AI exposure is diffused across construction loans, equity markets and working-capital revolver debt, and single-party risk limits will be contained.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Up about 170bp YTD per Goldman credit strategists (Oct 9). Volta's roughly 11% yield is about 300bp wider.
Goldman forecasts defaults staying elevated, with recoveries around $56 versus $64 in 2022.
Widest since at least 2009, up from 182bp in mid-September, per IFR.

crypto_views: Bitdeer (BTDR), a Bitcoin miner that operates data centers, is the data-center operator and lessor in the Volta Norway complex.
risk_factors: Best-efforts GPU tranche may be flexed wider, downsized or pushed into private credit if the Volta books do not clear.
GPU collateral may lose value faster than the six-year depreciation CoreWeave uses.
Risk shifting from banks to private credit funds and insurers, with indirect bank exposure flagged by the Bank of England.
Circular vendor financing, with Nvidia investing in Volta, which buys Nvidia chips.
Off-balance-sheet SPV debt at hyperscalers, including Moody's flag of $662B in hyperscaler lease commitments.
Rising leveraged loan defaults and falling recoveries.

tension_points.bull_case: Banks run originate-to-distribute and best-efforts syndication for a first-time unrated borrower is not unprecedented. Private credit and insurers keep funding AI, and Broadcom's Hock Tan says frontier labs can afford expensive financing. Anthropic is contracted for six years at the site.
tension_points.bear_case: Partial underwriting, syndication fatigue, SRTs, record CDS and an 11% yield show banks avoiding the risk. It shifts to private credit, with indirect bank exposure flagged by the Bank of England.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Volta's books closing 5pm ET Oct 14 with the GPU tranche flexed wider, downsized or pushed into private credit.

theme_stances.key_argument: Banks underwrite the cash-backed lease, sell the GPU risk best-efforts and hedge via CDS and SRTs, so they finance the AI boom without owning it.
theme_stances.evidence: JPM and Goldman will finance the AI boom; they just won't own it.
